Motor Performance & Characteristic Curves

Electromechanical behavior curves and real-time operational response analysis.

Illustrative/Simulated Data — Not Measured Experimental Results.
Experimental characteristic curves (Torque, Current, and Efficiency vs Load) require an attached dynamometer, RPM sensor, and shunt sensor. The curves below depict standard theoretical DC motor electromechanical characteristics for educational & validation reference. Live time-series graphs reflect real-time commanded output.
1. Speed vs Torque Curve
Linear speed drop as shaft torque increases to stall
2. Speed vs Mechanical Load
Rotational speed response across rated load %
3. Torque vs Mechanical Load
Direct linear torque progression with mechanical resistance
4. Efficiency vs Load Curve
Peak motor efficiency region (~60% rated load)
5. PWM Duty Cycle vs Speed Transfer
Deadband threshold, linear range, and saturation
6. Current vs Mechanical Load
Armature current rising from no-load to stall current
7. Live Commanded Speed vs Time
Real-time speed command history over the session (s)
8. Operating State vs Time
Step-response history of motor Run (1) vs Stop (0)
